subject: Processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer — Peregrine Q&A
messages:
From: Tim Sharp <security@peregrine-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anya Cole <anya.cole@peregrine-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Initial Qs — where our requests are executed / subprocessors / cross-border transfers

Jordan,

Thanks for the meeting yesterday. We are pulling together the list of clauses our procurement & security teams need answered before legal will move forward. High priority items for us: 1) exactly which geographic regions (cloud/edge) handle inference requests for the hosted product, 2) what subprocessors are involved (cloud providers, CDN, monitoring), and 3) whether customer data ever leaves the region selected (cross-border hops).

Can you provide concise, evidence-backed answers we can include in our risk assessment? Also note: Peregrine requires a guarantee of no transfers outside the EU for EU-only customers unless explicit authorization is provided.

Appreciate a short write-up and any supporting artifacts (subprocessor roster, DPA language).

—Tim
Tim Sharp
Head of Information Security
Peregrine Analytics

Subject: Re: Initial Qs — processing/execution map + subprocessor list (concise)

Tim / team — below is a concise, evidence-oriented summary you can use in your assessment. I've attached two items: a one-page geo-processing overview (geo-processing-overview.pdf) and our subprocessor roster (subprocessor-roster-202606.pdf).

1) Execution locations by product tier
- Hosted (Redwood API): customers choose an execution region at account creation/route configuration. Primary regions currently supported: us-east-1 (AWS), us-west-2 (AWS), europe-west1 (GCP), europe-north1 (GCP). For hosted customers who select an EU region, inference execution is pinned to EU compute by default and we do not route hosted inference to non-EU compute unless explicitly configured.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Dedicated pools are provisioned in the customer-specified region and are single-tenant for compute. We can provision EU-only Dedicated pools (contractually restricted).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Control plane remains with Redwood, but runtime and model execution occur in the customer-managed environment (VPC or on-prem) and never transit Redwood-managed infrastructure unless the customer elects hybrid telemetry or support access.

2) Subprocessors (examples & roles) — see attached roster for full list and signed agreements
- Cloud compute: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1, europe-north1) — used for hosted runtime and some Dedicated offerings.
- Edge/CDN: Fastly (for optional streaming endpoints / static assets).
- Observability/monitoring: Datadog (telemetry ingestion; telemetry can be disabled for Private deployments).
- Storage/archives: Google Cloud Storage (regional buckets) and S3 (regional) for ephemeral request logs and model artifacts.
- Infra security & secrets: HashiCorp Vault (managed service) and integrated KMS per customer where required.

All subprocessors included in the roster have executed our Vendor Security Questionnaire and have contractual data processing terms that reflect the EU Standard contractual clauses where applicable. We update the roster quarterly and include the version date in the attachment filename.

3) Cross-border transfers and controls
- Hosted EU accounts: by default, for accounts configured with an EU execution region, inference execution (and ephemeral request processing) occurs within EU compute. We do not export raw customer content to non-EU regions for processing unless you: (a) change the route/region configuration, (b) explicitly opt into cross-region fallback (we document and require explicit consent), or (c) use a Dedicated/Private configuration that you have provisioned outside the EU.
- Caching and ephemeral storage: Short-lived caches (prefix caches, KV caches) are kept in the same region as execution and have TTLs measured in seconds/minutes for inference sessions. Persistence of logs/artifacts follows retention policies (below) and is stored in regional buckets unless otherwise requested.
- Fallback behavior: If an EU region is fully saturated, our policy is to route to the next-compatible EU region where possible. Cross-region fallback to non-EU compute only occurs under documented and consented escalation (e.g., customer-authorized burst to US) and we provide alerts + opt-in in the Console.

4) Retention and deletion
- Short-term inference logs: retained for up to 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring. Customers can shorten this via account settings.
- Persistent artifacts (aggregated metrics, model telemetry): retained for analytics with pseudonymization where possible; retention windows are configurable per contract.
- Deletion upon request: For hosted accounts, data deletion requests are executed within 30 days (indexing and replication windows included). For Dedicated/Private, deletion timing depends on how the environment is provisioned — Dedicated we typically complete within 7–30 days; Private is customer-controlled for on-prem.

5) Evidence and contractual options
- We can provide: quarterly subprocessor roster (attached), sample DPA with EU-only processing clause (sample-dpa.pdf), SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer use, and a one-page execution map (attached).
- For EU-only residency guarantees: recommended approach is Hosted with EU-region pin + DPA clause specifying no transfers out of EU without written consent, or Dedicated provisioned in EU with contractual SOW. For the highest assurance, Private VPC or on-prem deployment avoids Redwood-managed compute entirely.

If it helps, I'm happy to produce a short one-page statement you can include in your procurement packet saying: "Peregrine account configured for europe-west1 execution; Redwood will not transfer inference requests outside the EU unless explicitly authorized in writing."

Next steps: let me know which artifacts you'd like (SOC 2, roster, DPA) and we'll push them to your shared Drive link.

—Rishi Malhotra
Dir, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

If you can bundle those three items, we can run them through our procurement queue this week. Also, for the EU-only guarantee language I mentioned earlier, please include suggested contract wording.

—Tim
